lead.headline: A Home-Made Shield for India’s Chickens
lead.deck: India’s first bird flu vaccine for chickens could cost 1 to 2 rupees a dose.
body: Eggs and chicken are part of many family meals in India. On Friday, India launched its first home-made vaccine to protect chickens from bird flu.

Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan unveiled it in Bhopal, where scientists at a government lab spent three years making it. A vaccine trains a body to fight a germ. This one holds bird flu viruses made harmless with chemicals. They cannot multiply, but they teach a chicken’s body to fight the real virus.

That matters, because this bird flu can kill almost every bird it infects. India has had more than 500 bird flu outbreaks since 2006, and farms have often had to cull, or kill, whole flocks to stop the spread.

Each dose may cost just 1 to 2 rupees, and officials expect the vaccine to help more than 90 lakh poultry farmers. A lakh is 100,000. Bird flu infects people only rarely, says the World Health Organization.

lead.why: A cheap vaccine could protect farm birds and the families who earn their living raising them, instead of losing whole flocks to the virus.

world.headline: A Small Country Speaks Up for Families Far Away
world.deck: The world’s top court has ruled on what Myanmar did to the Rohingya.
body: Can a small country stand up for people far away? In 2019, The Gambia, a small country in West Africa, took Myanmar, in Asia, to the International Court of Justice, the United Nations’ top court in The Hague, the Netherlands.

The case was about the Rohingya, a Muslim minority group in Myanmar. In 2017, Myanmar’s army carried out a crackdown, a harsh use of force, and about 700,000 Rohingya fled to Bangladesh. About 1.2 million now live in camps there.

On Thursday, the judges decided by 9 votes to 6 that Myanmar committed genocide, the crime of trying to destroy a whole group of people. The UN says it is the first ruling like this against a country under the Genocide Convention. Myanmar has said it was answering attacks on police posts.
The court ordered Myanmar to pay compensation, let the Rohingya return home safely if they choose, and reunite families.

us.headline: Measles Is Spreading Again in America
us.deck: The country has lost the status it held for 26 years.
body: Measles is one of the most catching illnesses known. Where people are not protected, one sick person can pass it to 12 to 18 others.

For 26 years, the United States counted measles as eliminated, which means it was not spreading inside the country. On Tuesday, a health group for the Americas said that is no longer true, because the virus has spread without a break for at least 12 months. America has had more than 5,400 cases this year.

The answer, health officials say, is the MMR vaccine. Two doses give about 97% protection. Last school year, 92% of kindergartners were vaccinated, below the 95% needed for herd immunity, when so many people are protected that a germ struggles to spread.
us.why: When enough people in a town are vaccinated, measles struggles to spread, and that helps protect everyone around us.

india.headline: Bike Taxis Can Keep Rolling in Karnataka
india.deck: The Supreme Court turned down the state’s request to ban them.
body: How do people in your family get around town? In Bengaluru and the rest of Karnataka, many ride bike taxis. They book a ride on an app such as Ola, Uber or Rapido, then hop on the back of a motorcycle.

Karnataka’s government wanted to stop these rides. It raised worries about passenger safety, insurance and traffic jams. But in January, the Karnataka High Court, the state’s top court, ruled that motorcycles can be registered to carry paying passengers. The state may set conditions, it said, but cannot refuse permits just because a vehicle is a motorcycle.

The state then appealed, or asked the Supreme Court, India’s highest court, to change that ruling. On Friday, two Supreme Court judges turned the appeal down. They noted that motorcycles take up less road space than cars and are affordable.
The app companies say about 4.5 lakh passengers in Karnataka use bike taxis.
india.why: Courts check state governments: Karnataka can make bike taxis safer with rules, but it cannot ban them just for being motorcycles.

lines.text: Good morning, and welcome to The Breakfast Table for Saturday, November 21. Today: a tiny shield for India’s chickens, an illness spreading again in America, and a court case about bike taxis.
Let’s start with chickens. What happened in India?
On Friday, India launched its first home-made vaccine to protect chickens from bird flu. Scientists at a government lab in Bhopal spent three years making it.
How does a vaccine actually help a chicken?
A vaccine trains a body to fight a germ. This one holds bird flu viruses made harmless with chemicals. They cannot multiply, but they still teach a chicken’s body how to fight the real virus.
Why does that matter so much to farmers?

This kind of bird flu can kill almost every bird it infects, and farms have often had to cull, or kill, whole flocks to stop it spreading. Each dose may cost just 1 to 2 rupees, and officials expect it to help more than 90 lakh poultry farmers. A lakh is 100,000.
Next, America. What is going on with measles?

For 26 years, the United States counted measles as eliminated, which means it was not spreading inside the country. Now a health group for the Americas says that is no longer true, because the virus has kept spreading without a break for at least 12 months.
Why does measles spread so easily?
It is one of the most catching illnesses known. Where people are not protected, one sick person can pass it to 12 to 18 others. This year, America has had more than 5,400 cases.
So what keeps people safe?

Health officials say it is the MMR vaccine. Two doses give about 97% protection. When enough people are protected, a germ struggles to spread. That is called herd immunity, and it needs 95% vaccinated. Last school year, 92% of kindergartners were.
And finally, back to India. What is a bike taxi?
In Karnataka, many people book a ride on an app, then hop on the back of a motorcycle. The app companies say about 4.5 lakh passengers there use bike taxis.
Why did that end up in court?

Karnataka’s government wanted to stop the rides, because of worries about safety, insurance and traffic jams. But a state court ruled that the state may set conditions, and cannot refuse permits just because a vehicle is a motorcycle.
So the state asked a higher court?

Yes, the Supreme Court, India’s highest court. On Friday, two judges turned the appeal down. They noted that motorcycles take up less road space than cars and are affordable. So bike taxis can keep rolling.
How much may each dose of India’s new chicken vaccine cost?
1 to 2 rupees The paper says each dose may cost just 1 to 2 rupees.
For how many years had the United States counted measles as eliminated?
26 years The US had held the status for 26 years.
How can getting a vaccine help the people around you, and not just you?
That’s all for today. Thanks for riding along with us, and enjoy your weekend!
